AgentPro is your call-center softphone. This guide explains every screen and feature, all on your phone. Reach each tool from the row of tabs along the bottom of the app — swipe that row sideways to see them all: Dialpad, Disp, Campaign, Contacts, Panel, History, Settings, CDR, Agent, Wallboard and Minutes.

Your SIP extension appears at the top of the Dialpad with a green “Connected” badge when it is registered. The line underneath shows the server and transport in use (for example host:5061 via TLS). To view or edit your account open Settings ▸ Accounts, or Settings ▸ PBX & Connection settings ▸ Manage SIP Account.

AgentPro can hold several SIP accounts at once, and each account keeps its OWN PBX connection, dispositions, campaign list, contacts and speed-dials — so switching account swaps the whole workspace, not just the line.

Switch the active account in either place:
• Tap the account number at the top of the Dialpad → pick another account (the active one is marked ●).
• Settings ▸ Accounts → tap an account to make it active.

The change takes effect everywhere instantly — no restart. Use “Add account” to sign in to another extension.

Type a number and tap the green button to call. During a call the keypad sends DTMF tones for IVR menus. The ⟳ button clears the field and the ⌫ button deletes one digit.

• Uptime — how long the app has stayed registered.
• Idle — time since your last call.
• Speed-dial chips under the number field place a one-tap call to a saved contact; tap “+” to add one, long-press a chip to remove it.
• Tap the account number at the top to switch between your accounts.

These toggles sit in the bar under the keypad:

• DND (Do Not Disturb) — silently declines every incoming call. Use the clock icon to switch DND off automatically after a set number of minutes.
• Auto Answer — answers incoming calls automatically after a short delay (handy with a headset).
• Auto Disp — opens the disposition dialog automatically at the end of each call.

The call screen shows the live audio codec in use (for example PCMA 8 kHz) and the media-encryption status in the header, so you can confirm call quality and security at a glance. Use Mute, Speaker, Hold and the keypad (DTMF) as usual.

Records the outcome of each call (Interested, No answer, Callback, …). The list is searchable and sortable, and the Export button saves everything to an Excel (.xlsx) file you can share. Each account keeps its own dispositions.

Import a contact list from an Excel (.xlsx) file — columns are detected automatically, or download the blank template first. Tap Start to dial contacts one after another with a delay between calls; Stop pauses the loop. You can also call, edit or delete any row by hand, then export the updated list.
A simple contact manager. Import or export contacts as Excel, search the list, and tap a row to call or edit it. This list is kept separate from your phone’s native contacts.

Shows your colleagues’ extensions and whether each one is idle, ringing or on a call — live, through the PBX (AMI) connection. As a supervisor you can Listen, Whisper or Barge into an active call from here. Requires the PBX settings to be filled in (see Settings).
Your recent calls — incoming, outgoing and missed — newest first. A red badge over the tab counts the calls you missed. Tap any entry to call the person back or to open its details.

Browse the PBX call history for the whole system. Choose a date range and/or search by number, then view the records or export them to Excel. Open the in-app PBX Page to listen to call recordings stored on the server.

Log in or out of the call-center queues with your extension and set yourself Paused or Available. Your live state and a session timer are shown. You set your extension, protocol (PJSIP/SIP) and the queue names directly on this screen; the “＋” button adds a queue. Needs the AMI connection from PBX settings.

A real-time call-center dashboard. Every queue shows a card with the number of waiting calls, logged-in agents, free agents, the longest current wait and the average talk time — refreshed automatically every few seconds.

Measures how many OUTBOUND minutes each extension used over a period, read from the PBX call records.

• Pick a start and end date-time.
• Leave the extensions box empty to auto-detect every active extension, or type specific ones.
• The Min/Max digit filter counts only real outside numbers (by how many digits they have).
• Each extension shows Talk minutes (answered time) and Call minutes (including ringing).
• Set an alarm limit to flag any extension that went over, and export the table to Excel.

• Accounts — add, switch between or remove your SIP accounts.
• PBX & Connection settings — the PBX host and AMI port/username/password, the supervisor feature codes (Listen / Whisper / Barge), the HTTPS API login for CDR & recordings, and the web-GUI login for the in-app PBX Page. A banner shows which account you are editing — each account has its own PBX. These power the Panel, CDR and Wallboard tabs. Use “Test Connection” before you save.
• App settings (advanced) — audio, video, network and developer options.
• User Guide — this manual.
• Export configuration (encrypted) — save all your settings and accounts to a password-protected file you can move to another phone.
• Import configuration — restore that file; the app restarts to apply it.
• Quit app — fully closes AgentPro and stops the background service.

Your PBX passwords are encrypted on the device. To move to a new phone, use Settings ▸ Export configuration: it bundles every setting and account into one password-protected file. On the new phone choose Import configuration and enter the same password. Keep that password safe — without it the backup cannot be opened.

• A green “Connected” badge means you are registered; red or grey means a problem — check your internet and the PBX settings.
• One-way or no audio is usually a NAT/firewall issue — confirm the STUN/network settings with your administrator.
• Do not register the same SIP extension on two devices at once; it breaks call routing.
• Panel / CDR / Agent / Wallboard / Minutes stay empty until the PBX connection details are entered in Settings.
• Just switched account and a screen still looks empty? Each account has its own PBX — open PBX settings while that account is active and fill it in.
